The 10-minute lesson on context and memory (O3) is written, along with a five-item quiz and its key. I didn't open the lesson in a browser, and I haven't run any of the format checks on the files.

- **Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`. It starts with a recall question on who runs tools, then covers three ideas. Each has a numbered trace with token counts, in the example-first style your preferences ask for.
  - **What the model sees:** the program re-sends the whole history on every call, so the context only grows and you pay for every token each time. In the trace, three calls read 6,200 tokens in total.
  - **Notes between sessions:** the context is gone when a session ends, so a saved note about a student's training status is loaded back into the next one. The lesson says the note costs about 60 tokens, against 20,000 to replay old chats.
  - **Retrieval:** a search tool pulls a few small chunks of a long manual into the context instead of pasting the whole thing. The lesson works this out as roughly 67 times fewer tokens.

  It also has two "common mix-up" boxes and two practice checks with instant feedback.
- **Quiz:** `quizzes/0002.json` (key in `keys/0002.json`). I haven't shown you any answers. Ask me for it when you want to try it.
- **Workspace:** I created `RESOURCES.md` with the three Anthropic sources I read, and added a line to `NOTES.md`.

**Things to know:**
- **Sources:** I only read search-result summaries, not the full pages, because the results came back truncated. The numbers in the examples (token counts, manual sizes) are made up for teaching.
- **Missing pieces:** I found no community link to put in "Go further", so it points you to your design review instead. I also didn't write a cheat sheet.
- **Misconception id:** the quiz reuses `M3` from quiz 0001, which covers the idea that memory is automatic.
- **Earlier quiz:** quiz 0001 (submissions `s1` and `s2`) is still ungraded.

Do you want me to grade quiz 0001 next, or would you rather take quiz 0002 first?
